title: Former gas works secures £3m bridge loan for site clean-up
summary:
A former gas works site in Tonbridge, Kent has secured £3 million in bridging finance from Secure Trust Bank Business Finance to fund remediation works ahead of a planned 144-apartment development. Real estate advisory firm FRP arranged the 18-month facility, structured at 44% loan-to-value.

title: Assetz Capital provides £5.5m for Liverpool apartment scheme
summary:
Assetz Capital has provided £5.5 million in development finance to convert a vacant former college building in Woolton, Liverpool, into 18 residential apartments. The 18-month facility, structured at approximately 58% loan-to-value, will fund demolition and construction of a mixed-unit development.

title: Housebuilder warns first-time buyer scheme may delay sales
summary:
Gleeson Homes has warned that the government's Your First Home scheme could postpone demand and increase cancellations before its April 2027 launch. The affordable housing specialist anticipates a weaker first half as potential buyers delay purchases to access the 20% equity loan programme.

title: Government allows gas boiler exemptions in new homes policy
summary:
The UK Government has amended its Future Homes Standard policy to allow exemptions for gas boiler installations in new homes under exceptional circumstances. Local councils will be granted powers to waive requirements for low-carbon heating systems in specific cases, with implementation scheduled for March 2025.

The post Government allows gas boiler exemptions in new homes policy appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Investment property purchases drive bridging finance growth
summary:
Investment property purchases accounted for 23% of bridging transactions between July and September, up from 18% in the previous quarter. Contributors lent £181.8 million during the third quarter, a 5% increase from the previous quarter, though total lending remained 13.2% below the same period last year.

title: Compliance concerns drive landlords to letting agents
summary:
Compliance and legal complexity have emerged as the primary reason landlords engage letting agents, according to new research. The survey found that two-thirds of landlords have altered their property management arrangements in the past two years.

title: Mortgage brokers cite solicitor delays as top frustration
summary:
More than half of mortgage brokers identify chasing solicitors for progress updates as their primary frustration with the conveyancing process, according to new industry polling. The survey found 56% cited having to chase solicitors as their biggest challenge during property transactions.

title: Skipton Building Society joins digital homebuying platform
summary:
Skipton Building Society has joined the National Property Transaction Network, a digital platform designed to connect estate agents, mortgage lenders and conveyancers throughout the homebuying process. The platform aims to enable property and financial information to be captured once and securely shared between relevant parties during a transaction.

title: Lendhub provides £2.1m for Surrey residential scheme
summary:
Lendhub has provided £2.1m in development finance for a 15-unit residential scheme in Addlestone, Surrey, combining the refurbishment of an existing apartment block with new construction. The 18-month facility covers acquisition and refurbishment of 12 flats plus construction of three additional units through a rear extension.

title: Somerset holiday lodge park secures £2.69m refinance
summary:
A mixed-use holiday lodge park near Bridgwater, Somerset, has secured £2.69 million in refinancing from Atom bank, arranged by Unicorn Capital Advisory. The secured term loan completed on 16 October 2026.
